searchText: The consensus-specs use the `get_pow_block` function, I'm wondering how we distringuish between a PoW block (execution block, pre-merge) and a PoS block (execution block, post-merge). On the same thread, I wonder about the maximum loops of the `for` loop in `get_pow_block_at_terminal_total_difficulty`. My understanding is that if `get_pow_block` only returns pre-merge execution blocks, then it's only ever going to return not-`None` on the first iteration. If `get_pow_block` returns post-merge execution blocks (i.e., not PoW) then it could run any number of times (bounded by `len(pow_chain)`). The name `get_pow_block` rather refers to the content of returned data than to the consensus mechanism that is responsible for the block creation. So, it should return `PowBlock` structure in response to whatever block hash is requested (if the corresponding block exists). The existing `eth_getBlockByHash` method is suggested as an implementation of `get_pow_block` abstraction. Hello wrinkle brained devs. Can anyone give me a very rough ETA for the merge? I know about the github 'to-do' list but am far too smooth brained to understand how long the remaining tasks could take. TIA I'm interested in this too. I understand that this channel is mainly for technical discussions pertaining to the merge, but there's no good place to ask this question elsewhere, unless you guys would recommend another channel? We're working on it 🙂 We'll probably can give better estimates in two/three weeks from now. I wouldn't expect the merge to happen before Q1 2022 due to testing, etc. So you should not consider going and buying mining hardware at this point anymore. and to followup. The abstract pow_chain and the for loop get_pow_block are just to show retrieval functionality. Definitely suggest using json rpc method available!
